speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the MRI of the spinal cord is normal, we must consider lesions outside the spine or systemic causes. Have you noticed any muscle weakness in your arms or hands, and have you experienced any changes in your vision or hearing?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain (Whole)
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C)

The MRI findings of atrophy in the cerebellum, brainstem, and basal ganglia combined with your progressive gait instability, early urinary incontinence, and dysarthria strongly suggest a neurodegenerative condition affecting multiple systems. Given the prominence of cerebellar signs (ataxia) alongside autonomic dysfunction, this pattern is most consistent with Multiple System Atrophy, specifically the cerebellar subtype (MSA-C).
